data.exact_reserve_text: In 2015, there has been an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 0.6m (2014:GBP 3.8m) due primarily to a reduction in claims estimates as uncertainty around catastrophe exposure unwinds.

prior_year_events.impact_description: reduction in respect of reserves required for Superstorm Sandy, leading to a release of reserves in 2014.

data.standardized_narrative: For the 2015 financial year, Syndicate 6103 reported an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 0.6 million, indicating a release of prior year reserves. This favorable development was primarily attributed to a reduction in claims estimates as uncertainty around catastrophe exposure unwound. No specific named events were cited as causes for the 2015 reserve movement, though Superstorm Sandy (2012) had led to a significant release in 2014.
raw_causal_phrases: reduction in claims estimates as uncertainty around catastrophe exposure unwinds
data.data_quality_notes: The claims development triangle on page 28 is very limited, showing only three underwriting years (2013-2015). The explicit gross prior year development figure from the narrative on page 28 was used as the primary source. The report mentions 'RITC 2012 YOA commuted into Syn 2791' on page 26, which could distort claims development tables, but an explicit gross PYD figure was available.
